entry.question:
## Physical scenario

Determine the self-inductance of a toroidal solenoid with cross-sectional area \( A \) and mean radius \( r \), closely wound with \( N \) turns of wire on a nonmagnetic core. Assume that \( B \) is uniform across a cross section (that is, neglect the variation of \( B \) with distance from the toroid axis).

## Question

Determine the self-inductance of a toroidal solenoid.

## Answer choices

- A: A: 22\ \mu\mathrm{H}

- B: B: 40\ \mu\mathrm{H}

- C: C: 75\ \mu\mathrm{H}

- D: D: 28\ \mu\mathrm{H}

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image illustrates a toroidal solenoid. It depicts a toroidal coil with multiple turns of wire, represented by purple loops wrapping around a beige torus. The direction of current, \(i\), is indicated by purple arrows along the wire.

Key elements include:

- A large arrow labeled \(r\) points radially outward from the center to the outer edge, indicating the radius.
- The top of the torus is labeled \(A\).
- Dashed lines with arrows show the direction of the magnetic field inside the toroid.

Text on the image reads:

"Number of turns = \(N\) (only a few are shown)"

The diagram conveys the basic structure and function of the toroidal solenoid, focusing on the current flow and magnetic field.
